numberItems.stem: During your inspection, what is the minimum tread depth for a **front** tire?
numberItems.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch in every major groove; other tires need 2/32 inch (p. 2-2).

numberItems.stem: What is the minimum tread depth for a tire that is **not** on the front (for example, a rear drive tire)?
numberItems.explanation: Tires other than front tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread; front tires need 4/32 inch in every major groove (p. 2-2).

numberItems.stem: Which tires are prohibited on the front wheels of a bus?
numberItems.explanation: Regrooved, recapped or retreaded tires are prohibited on the front wheels of a bus (p. 2-2).

numberItems.stem: Steering wheel play of more than how much can make the vehicle hard to steer?
numberItems.explanation: Steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees (about 2 inches at the rim of a 20-inch wheel) can make it hard to steer (p. 2-2).

numberItems.stem: A leaf spring has 8 leaves. How many missing leaves will put the vehicle out-of-service?
numberItems.explanation: If ¼ or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle is put out-of-service; ¼ of 8 is 2 (p. 2-3). Any defect can still be dangerous.

numberItems.stem: You use fusees as your warning devices for a parked vehicle. How many does the handbook list?
numberItems.explanation: Warning devices: 3 red reflective triangles, 6 fusees, or 3 liquid-burning flares (p. 2-4; the handbook prints "6 fuses").

numberItems.stem: According to Figure 2.5, what is normal oil pressure with the engine **idling**?
numberItems.explanation: Figure 2.5: 5–20 psi idling and 35–75 psi operating; low, dropping or fluctuating pressure means stop immediately (p. 2-5).

numberItems.stem: During the in-cab check in section 2.1, air pressure should build from ___ within 3 minutes.
numberItems.explanation: Section 2.1: air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes (p. 2-5). 85–100 psi in 45 seconds is the Air Brakes section's dual-system figure.

numberItems.stem: Where is governor cut-out usually, when you build air pressure during the inspection?
numberItems.explanation: Build the air pressure to governor cut-out, usually around 120–140 psi (p. 2-5).

numberItems.stem: Testing hydraulic brakes for leaks: after pumping the pedal 3 times, you apply firm pressure and hold it for how long?
numberItems.explanation: Pump the brake pedal 3 times, then apply firm pressure and hold for 5 seconds; the pedal should not move (p. 2-8).

numberItems.stem: To test the service brake stopping action, about how fast should you drive before pushing the brake pedal firmly?
numberItems.explanation: Drive about 5 mph and push the brake pedal firmly; pulling to one side or delayed stopping can mean brake trouble (p. 2-8).

numberItems.stem: You made your first cargo securement check. Now you drive slow roads at about 30 mph. When must you check the cargo again?
numberItems.explanation: After the first check within 50 miles, check every 150 miles or every 3 hours, whichever comes first (p. 2-8). At 30 mph, 3 hours (90 miles) comes first.

numberItems.stem: How long should you keep a copy of your vehicle inspection report in the vehicle?
numberItems.explanation: Keep a copy of your report in the vehicle for 1 day so the next driver can learn about any problems (p. 2-9).

numberItems.stem: During the walk-around, what color should the **rear** clearance and identification lights and rear reflectors be?
numberItems.explanation: Front clearance, identification lights and reflectors are amber; rear clearance and identification lights and rear reflectors are red (pp. 2-6 to 2-7).
